rule.title: Magic Bytes File Signature Verification on Uploads
rule.statement: Uploaded files must be verified by reading their initial magic byte signatures, never relying solely on the client-supplied MIME type or file extension.
rule.rationale: Attackers can rename malicious executables or HTML scripts to .pdf or .docx, bypassing extension checks and causing RCE or XSS.
rule.implementation_guidance: Inspect the first 4-8 bytes of the file buffer (e.g., %PDF- for PDF, PK for DOCX/XLSX) before passing to parsers.

forbidden.example: const isPdf = file.originalname.endsWith('.pdf'); // Dangerous client spoofing

source.book_title: Alice and Bob Learn Application Security
source.evidence_quote: Never trust the client-provided Content-Type or file extension. Verify the actual file content using magic bytes to ensure it matches the expected format.

rule.title: Strict File Size Limits and Memory Quotas
rule.statement: File upload endpoints must enforce a strict maximum file size limit (20MB) and total payload quota to prevent Denial of Service (DoS).
rule.rationale: Unbounded file uploads allow malicious users to exhaust server memory and disk space (Zip Bombs, huge PDFs), taking down the service.

forbidden.example: multer(); // Default with no file size limits

source.book_title: Alice and Bob Learn Application Security
source.section: Denial of Service via File Uploads
source.evidence_quote: Enforce strict size limits on uploaded files at the reverse proxy and application level to protect against memory exhaustion and storage starvation.
